sprint: Image Studio — Trim Picture was locked behind background removal. Reported: "ok while we wait the crop functionality of image studio seems to have broken can you check that." Reproduced first rather than guessed at: a fresh PictureStudio.open() renders the ✂️ Trim Picture tile with disabled===true, so a child who simply wants to crop a photo cannot, ever, without first tapping ✨ Remove Paper. ROOT CAUSE is a stale gate left behind by a shipped ship, not a broken crop: _refreshBgControls carried `_cropTile.disabled = !_bgRemovedImg`, written back when background removal ran automatically on every open() so a working buffer always existed by the time anyone reached for a tool. The later "Background Removal Is On-Demand, Never the Default" ship removed that auto-run without revisiting the gate, and since _workingBuffer/_bgRemovedImg were set ONLY by _onBgResult, every pixel tool silently inherited a dependency on a removal the child never asked for. Trimming a photo has nothing to do with removing its paper.
task:
THE FIX IS A FLAG SPLIT PLUS LAZY MATERIALIZATION, not merely a loosened gate. _bgRemovedImg keeps meaning "the canvas currently displayed and edited" — but a new, narrower _bgRemovalDone answers "did the worker actually run?", and that is what the Remove Paper tile, the Before/After compare wrap and the erase brush sub-panel key off, since none of the three mean anything without a genuine removal. Simply overloading _bgRemovedImg was considered and REJECTED: it would have made Remove Paper refuse to run after a plain trim, and un-hidden both the compare slider (where "before" and "after" would be the same picture) and the alpha-erase brush (with no removed alpha to erase).

New _ensureWorkingBuffer() materializes a mutable buffer on demand via the existing _bakeSourceForBg(), mints the matching canvas, and — deliberately — BAKES ROTATION AND FLIP exactly as _startBgRemoval already does, resetting _state.rotation/_state.flipH, because _screenToContent (which converts a drag box into buffer pixels) has always assumed an un-rotated buffer and carries the comment saying so. Two alternatives rejected here too: making _screenToContent rotation-aware (a screen-drawn box on a rotated picture is NOT axis-aligned in buffer space, so inverse-transforming its corners gives a wrong rectangle rather than a rotated one), and adding a doodle-remap-through-rotation subsystem (scope creep — the same drift is pre-existing on the removal path, so baking introduces no NEW class of bug; disclosed in the code comment rather than papered over). The bake is triggered from _toggleActiveTool on ENTERING crop rather than on the first drag, so the picture never visibly changes mid-gesture.

_startCropDrag and _autoCrop swap their `if(!_workingBuffer) return;` guards for _ensureWorkingBuffer(), so both Auto Crop and a hand-drawn box work from a cold open. _finishCropDrag now resolves coordinates against _workingBuffer (the space _cropPixelBuffer actually operates in — _bgRemovedImg is drawn FROM that buffer so the dimensions match, but the buffer is the source of truth) with a null guard, and its clamp fallback was SIMPLIFIED rather than extended: the original re-called _screenToContent with identical arguments when the first call returned null, which could only ever return null again. Crop gates become `_cropTile.disabled = !_origImg` and the Keep This / Trash It pair `!(_cropRect && _workingBuffer)`, so the actions arm exactly when there is genuinely something to act on.

Verified 23/23, zero page errors, via a new crop_fix_verify suite driving the real modal with real page.mouse drags across six sections: A — Trim is enabled on open with NO removal ever run, the compare slider and erase brush correctly stay hidden, its own sub-panel opens, and Keep This / Trash It / Undo Trim all start disabled; B — a real drag arms both actions, Keep This crops, Undo Trim becomes available, and still no removal was triggered; C — Trash It arms Undo the same way, likewise with no removal; D — Undo Trim reverts and disables itself, Trim stays enabled, and ✨ Remove Paper afterwards still runs a GENUINE removal that wakes the removal-gated UI; E — the round trip works on a ROTATED picture end to end, which is the bake proving itself; F — zero uncaught page errors. THREE TEST-SIDE FIXES, all disclosed, none of them app bugs: the four boot overlays (preload gate, Traveller Gateway tap-to-begin, Creation Flow, Magic Card) are REMOVED rather than class-hidden, because Playwright hit-tests real drags against them; two selectors of my own were wrong against source (.picture-studio-ba-compare, and .picture-studio-brush-panel — the child _refreshBgControls toggles — rather than the [data-tool="brush"] wrapper the active-tool CSS shows); and two places had to tap ← Back before reaching another tile, since Ship B contextual collapse correctly hides every non-active tool tile.

Regression: bg_default_verify 12/12 (the on-demand-removal ship own suite — the one this fix is most at risk of undoing, confirming removal still never auto-runs), image_studio_draw_verify 26/26, photo_via_studio_verify 8/8, fa_replace_everywhere_verify 22/22, and both goldenBuild suites PASS unchanged. renderer/slideRenderer.js is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship.
